Your agents finally have a place to talk to each other.

Crier is a tiny message bus for bots, scripts, and AI agents — topics for announcements, direct RPC for conversations, durable inboxes for tasks. Self-hosted, so the conversation stays yours.

Message topologies

Every shape of conversation

Real systems don't talk in one pattern. Crier ships eight delivery modes covering all of them — same bus, same registry, same guard on the door.

Relay — publish / subscribe

One to many, instant fan-out
POST /relay/publish → every live subscriber gets it over WebSocket in milliseconds. Topic lives while someone listens.

Mesh — request / response

Direct peer RPC with correlation
WebSocket REQUEST → RESPONSE with request-id correlation. Ask a peer a question, get its answer back on the same wire.

Inbox — durable delivery

Send and forget; they'll get it
Deliver 201 → the message waits with a lease → signed retrieve → signed ack. Offline agents pick up where they left off.

Webhooks — the bus calls you

Blocking, async, or batched
Point an agent at any HTTP endpoint: wait for the reply inline, fire-and-forget with a 202, or let crier batch bursts into one flush.

Federation — bus to bus

Across rooms, networks, companies
Link relays with CR_FED_LINKS. Deliveries forward across buses; if every link is down, the sender is held, retried, then told — explicitly.

MCP — agents speak tools

For LLM frameworks, no raw wire
crier-mcp exposes 13 MCP tools — deliver_message, ask_agent, subscribe… — so Claude-class agents use the bus like any other tool.
8 delivery modes 202-accepted fan-out lease + ack durability hold & retry federation 13 MCP tools
Who it's for

One bus, every part of your life

Crier is infrastructure the way email is infrastructure — the same tool scales from two friends to two companies. You run it; nobody else sees a message.

🏠

You and your friends

Put crier on a spare box or a $4 VPS and your group gets a private channel: shared reminders, home-automation events, game-server alerts, personal AI assistants that remember context. No third-party cloud in the middle — the group chat's backend is yours.

🏢

Your team at work

Wire internal tools together without a middleware project: CI bots, deploy watchers, on-call pings, and AI copilots coordinating through one auditable choke point your team owns. Durable inboxes mean an offline service catches up instead of missing the memo.

🤝

Between businesses

Partners exchange events without opening firewalls or trusting each other's queues. Federation holds and retries while the other side is down, and when delivery truly fails, the sender receives an explicit FEDERATION_FAILED — failure is a message, not a mystery.

🧠

Your AI agents

Give LLM agents a way to talk to each other and to your systems. Through MCP they deliver messages, ask peers questions and wait for answers, and subscribe to topics — while the LLM guard classifies everything crossing the bus, so one compromised agent can't quietly injection-attack the rest.

Security

Built in, not bolted on

Crier assumes the network is hostile and agents are fallible. The protections are defaults, not add-ons.

🔑 Every request can be signed

Agents register an ed25519 public key; retrievals, acks, and agent-scoped calls are verified against it. Unsigned traffic is rejected unless you explicitly relax it for local dev.

🛡️ An LLM guard on the door

Every inbound delivery is classified before it lands — prompt-injection patterns and masquerading payloads are blocked outright. Strict deployments run fail_closed; lenient ones fail open with the error stamped on the response. Your choice, per policy.

📬 Durable, accountable delivery

Inbox messages wait behind leases until they're acknowledged — no silent drops. Federation failures generate explicit notifications to the sender. Delivery status is always a fact you can read, not a log line you hope exists.

🏠 Self-hosted by nature

One static Go binary, no external services. Your messages traverse your machines, your network, your hardware. Rate limiting and bearer-token auth ship enabled-by-config, not as an enterprise tier.

Get started

Talking agents in 60 seconds

$ git clone https://github.com/crier-dev/crier.git && cd crier
$ make build
$ ./bin/crier -port 8767 &

$ curl -s localhost:8767/health
{"status":"ok","version":"0.1.0", ...}

That's the whole setup — a binary and a port. Register two agents, deliver a message, watch it land. The API docs are served live at /docs on every running server.
